title: Dedicated cluster capacity event: root-cause synthesis and mitigation catalog
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Synthesize findings from the recent dedicated-cluster capacity incidents into a compact mitigation catalog. Focus areas: noisy-tenant isolation heuristics, reservation sizing corrections, and burst-token policy redesign. Deliverables: prioritized action list, rough estimates, PR/owner mapping, and a consolidated runbook entry for on-call ops.
investigation_summary: Multiple capacity disruptions across two clusters were correlated to (1) emergent microbursts from a small set of tenants that exceeded observed historical variance, (2) reservations that were conservatively under-allocated after a recent promo-driven workload change, and (3) burst token logic that allowed sustained bursts without proper debt reconciliation. Diagnostics used: tenant-level per-second tail-latency histograms, KV-cache miss heatmaps, reservation allocation audit logs, and autoscaler event traces. No single bug was responsible; the outage was a compound failure of policy and telemetry coverage.

action_items: (A1) Implement tenant noise-fence: lightweight per-tenant moving-window score to tag and soft-quarantine noisy tenants for up to 15 minutes - owner: Marco Chen - estimate: 5

(A2) Reservation recalibration pass: build script to recompute 95th-percentile sustained throughput per tenant using last 30 days; propose new minimum reservation ramping formula - owner: DataInfra (Priya Rao) - estimate: 3

(A3) Burst policy rewrite: introduce 'burst-debt' accounting so sustained bursts consume reservation credit faster and trigger graceful shedding before eviction - owner: Runtime (Diego Alvarez) - estimate: 8

(A4) Telemetry gaps: add tenant-level rolling histograms for p50/p95/p99 latency and continuous KV-cache hit-rate, surface on console per-tenant page - owner: Observability (Lena Brooks) - estimate: 5

(A5) Synthetic validator: daily synthetic load job that replays sampled tenant traffic patterns to detect potential reservation deficit or burst-policy regressions - owner: SRE (Marcus Li) - estimate: 4

(A6) Runbook update: consolidate mitigation catalog and step-by-step actions (soft-quarantine, reservation bump, controlled throttling) into dedicated runbook; include checklist and rollback criteria - owner: Oncall (Aisha Patel) - estimate: 2
(A7) Canary controls: add deployment gate that simulates high variance traffic through the new burst-debt logic before global rollout - owner: CI/CD (Elena Park) - estimate: 3
acceptance_criteria: Telemetry: tenant-level histograms are ingesting and visible for 90% of active tenants
Policy: noisy-tenant score tags noisy tenants with >80% precision during synthetic testcases
Reservation: recalibration script produces recommendations and we have pilot of top-10 customers validated
Burst policy: burst-debt reduces sustained-threshold breaches by >=60% in canary region
Runbook: oncall can run the catalog end-to-end in <= 25 minutes in drill
notes: Design tradeoff: aggressive noisy-tenant fencing reduces blast radius but increases false positives; initial approach is soft-quarantine (deny-burst but leave baseline traffic).
We should avoid instantaneous reservation bumps for safety; prefer staged ramp with 'reservation-probe' traffic to validate headroom.
Customer communication: CS draft under PM review - include temporary rate-limits and expected timeline for permanent fixes.
Long-lead: research a predictive reservation shrinker that uses short-term exponential smoothing to preempt microbursts - backlog candidate
